question.text: What is the root of the function $f(x)=\dfrac{2x}{5} - 3?$
question.explanation:
The roots are the solutions to the equation $f(x)=0,$ which we solve as follows:

\begin{align} f(x) &= 0 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2x}{5} - 3 &=0\\[5pt] \dfrac{2x}{5} &= 3\\[5pt] 2x &= 15\\[5pt] x & = \dfrac{15}{2} \end{align}

Therefore, the function has the single root $x= \dfrac{15}{2}.$
